fields.features_heading: Inside the Spelling Quiz Emergent Builds
fields.features_subheading: Emergent writes the questions from your list. The app grades every letter and keeps each attempt, wrong spellings included.
fields.feature_1:
Three question formats from one word list

Paste this week's words and Emergent drafts a question for each. Students pick the right spelling from four, type the word from a short clue, or find the misspelled word.
fields.feature_2:
Typed words graded letter for letter

A typed answer counts only when every letter matches, so recieve is marked wrong. At the end, each student sees a score and the right spelling of each word they missed.
fields.feature_3:
The misspelling saved as it was typed

Every attempt is stored in a database you own, with the student, the word, and the spelling they entered. Seeing seperate typed by six students says more than a red mark.
fields.feature_4:
One word per screen for young spellers

Kids get one word per screen on a tablet or phone, with a large text box and a progress bar. A 15-word pretest fits into the first ten minutes of a Monday spelling lesson.
fields.feature_5:
Emails to parents, alerts to teachers

Email each parent the words their child missed, or post a class summary to a teacher's Slack channel. A reminder can reach anyone who has not taken Friday's spelling test.
fields.feature_6:
Your school's domain, your code

Run the quiz on your own domain, which is included in Emergent and uses credits. On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and keep it for next year.

fields.tab_content_1:
Practice lists hold only the words each child missed

Every Monday, 48 third graders in 2 classes at Pellbridge Elementary take a 15-word pretest on a tablet. Each child's practice list holds only the words they missed, and Friday's test uses the full list again. This week, 7 of 48 spelled all 15 on Monday, and 29 of 48 did on Friday.
fields.tab_content_2:
From 18 club members, 4 qualify for the district bee

The Duskmoor Middle School spelling bee club has 18 members, who practice in 25-word rounds. Each word shows up as a definition and a sentence with a blank, and the student types it, so one wrong letter marks it wrong. After 3 rounds, the 4 top scorers qualified for the district bee, led by Isla Lunden with 24 of 25.
fields.tab_content_3:
Of 27 fifth graders, 14 slipped on doubled consonants

Ms. Penry's class of 27 fifth graders at Bellcroft Elementary takes a 20-word quiz in which every word is tagged with the spelling rule it tests. Sorted by rule, the misses showed that 14 of 27 students got at least one doubled consonant wrong, as in beginning or occurred. That rule became next week's mini-lesson.
fields.tab_content_4:
Every score of 17 or better emails the recruiter

Front-desk applicants at Ozwell Staffing take a 20-word spelling check of office words such as receive, schedule, and separate. A score of 17 or more passes, and the recruiter gets an email with the applicant's name and score. Last month, 41 of 64 applicants passed and moved to a phone interview the same week.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Spelling Quiz
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a spelling quiz that grades each word fairly and shows which spellings to teach again.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Choose a format for each word
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Write clues that point to one word
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Build wrong options from real errors
fields.howto_step_1_des: Take the words from this week's phonics pattern or reading, not a random list. A third-grade list of 15 words fits a Monday pretest and a Friday test. Paste the list into your prompt, and Emergent writes the questions.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Picking the right spelling from four options suits younger children who are still learning to type. Typing the word from a clue asks students to produce every letter themselves. Mix both in one quiz if the class has a range of spellers.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A typed question needs a clue only one word can answer. Pair a short meaning with an example in use, such as "We left ___ coats by the door." A clue that fits their, there, and they're equally will mark correct spellings wrong.
fields.howto_step_4_des: For pick-the-spelling questions, use the misspellings students write in their own work, such as recieve or seperate. Random letter swaps are easy to rule out. Keep all four options the same length so the right one does not stand out.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Settle the edge cases before anyone takes the quiz: whether capital letters matter, and whether a British spelling earns credit. Then set the score bands, such as 0 to 9, 10 to 13, and 14 to 15 out of 15.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Try it, then hand it to two spellers
fields.howto_step_6_des: Work through the quiz on the tablet or phone students will use. Then give it to one strong speller and one who struggles. Fix any clue they read two ways and any option that no one picks, then open it to the class.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Sort the misses by word and by rule
fields.howto_step_7_des: When the quiz closes, sort the answers by word to find the hardest spellings, then by rule to find the pattern behind them. Teach that pattern next, and put the missed words back on next week's list to check they stuck.

faq_plan.a: A spelling quiz is a short test of whether someone can write a word with every letter in the right order. The question gives a clue, such as a meaning, the word used in context, or four versions of the word, and the answer is either right or wrong. The results show which words, and which patterns, need more practice.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a spelling quiz?
faq_plan.a: Pick 10 to 15 words your students have studied, choose a question format for each, and decide whether capital letters count. With Emergent's AI survey builder, you describe the quiz in a prompt, paste the word list, and get a working app that grades every word and saves each attempt.

faq_plan.q: What should a spelling quiz maker let me control for a class?
faq_plan.a: It should let you set the word list and the grading rules, and it should show you each student's misspelling as typed. A tool that only reports right or wrong hides the pattern: seperate and separete point to different gaps. Being able to tag each word with its spelling rule makes the results easier to teach from.

faq_plan.q: How many words should a spelling quiz for kids have?
faq_plan.a: Keep it to about 10 words for first and second graders and 15 for third grade and up. Show large type and one word at a time. A pretest and a retest of the same list in one week show progress more clearly than one long test.

faq_plan.q: Can I make a free spelling quiz for my class?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent is free to start, and the free tier covers building and publishing. No response caps apply either, even with every class in the school taking the quiz in one week.

faq_plan.q: Do spelling quiz questions need to be read aloud?
faq_plan.a: No. A short meaning plus an example sentence with the word missing tells students which word to write without any sound. For a dictation test, read each word aloud in class while students type their answers on their own screens.

faq_plan.q: Should students see the spelling quiz questions and answers right after they finish?
faq_plan.a: Yes, for practice quizzes. Show each missed word with the student's spelling beside the correct one while the attempt is fresh. For a graded test that another class will take later, hold the answers until everyone has finished.

faq_plan.q: Which words belong on a spelling quiz for adults at work?
faq_plan.hint: Which is the correct spelling quiz?
faq_plan.a: Use the words people in that job write every day: for a front desk, words such as schedule and accommodate. Pull them from real emails or forms the team sends. A 20-word check is long enough to see a pattern and short enough to finish in a few minutes.

faq_plan.q: Does spell-check on a tablet give away the answers on a spelling quiz?
faq_plan.a: It can. The browser's spellcheck setting defines whether the element may be checked for spelling errors, and an answer box can be marked to skip it. MDN adds that this attribute is merely a hint for the browser. Test the quiz on the tablets your students use, and when you prompt Emergent, ask for answer boxes with spellcheck turned off.

faq_plan.q: How can I track spelling quiz scores for each student over the year?
faq_plan.a: Save every attempt with its date and the spelling entered, then compare the same words across weeks. In an app Emergent builds, that data lives in a database you own. Sort it by student or by spelling rule whenever you plan a lesson.

quiz.title: Spelling Quiz: Can You Pick the Right Spelling of 8 Words?
quiz.intro: Eight words with doubled letters, silent letters, and tricky vowels. Pick the correct spelling for each; your score and a tip for every word show at the end.

questions.text: The hotel can ___ 200 guests. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Accommodate has two c's and two m's. Picture a room big enough to hold both pairs.

source.quote: If you accommodate, you are making an adjustment to suit a particular purpose

questions.text: Keep the raw chicken ___ from the salad. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: There is a rat in separate: sep, a, rat, e. The letter right after the p is an a, not an e.

source.quote: Things that are separate are kept apart from other things

questions.text: Food and water are ___ for every living thing. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: One c and two s's, like a shirt with one collar and two sleeves.

source.quote: certain things are necessary for survival: food, water, shelter

questions.text: I will ___ be at the game on Saturday. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Definitely is built on finite, so the letter after the n is an i, never an a.

source.quote: Use definitely to describe something you

questions.text: The drummer kept a steady ___. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Rhythm uses y as its only vowel: r, h, y, t, h, m. The h appears twice.

source.quote: Use the noun rhythm to refer to the regular pattern of something in a cycle

questions.text: Did the mistake ___ you in front of the class? Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Embarrass doubles both the r and the s, which is the part people drop.

source.quote: If you embarrass someone, you make them feel self-conscious

questions.text: A solar eclipse is a rare ___. Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: Two c's, two r's, and an ending of ence, not ance. The r doubles when occur takes the ending.

source.quote: An occurrence is an instance of something or a time when something happens

questions.text: Did you ___ my email this morning? Which spelling is correct?
questions.explanation: After a c, the e comes before the i, as in receive, ceiling, and receipt.

source.quote: Receive means to get or accept

results.title: Keep Practicing
results.description: Each of these 8 words hides a trap that is easy to miss. Read the tip for each one you missed, write the word out three times, and take the quiz again tomorrow to see what stuck.

results.title: Solid Speller
results.description: You know the common traps and missed a few doubled letters or vowel swaps. Check the tips for the words you missed; the pattern behind each one shows up in other words too.

results.title: Spelling Pro
results.description: You spotted the right spelling almost every time, doubled letters and all. Try writing your own list of tricky words and testing a friend, a class, or your team with it.
